clue.text: Get a car and master the smallest points

blocks.note: the Mini is a small British car
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Buy a car and become an expert in the finest details.
explanation.definitionFit: Minima is the Latin plural of minimum, the lowest values or points on a curve or scale.

clue.text: A shabby experience to keep you punctual

definitions.note: A purpose phrase stands for the noun, fair because standard clock time exists precisely to keep everyone on schedule.

blocks.note: mean can describe something poor or shabby in appearance
a time is an experience, as in 'we had a good time'

explanation.surface: An unpleasant ordeal that at least teaches you to turn up on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean time is the averaged clock time, as in Greenwich Mean Time, the standard by which Britain sets its clocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean time is the uniform standard reckoning of hours used for clocks, the reference that keeps people prompt.

clue.text: It's crazy to produce a bird

blocks.note: a nut is a crazy person, and nutty means crazy
to hatch is to produce, as in hatching a plan

explanation.surface: It would be madness to try to create a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small woodland songbird that climbs tree trunks head-first.

clue.text: People get around to help a young girl

indicators.note: people getting around something surround it, so their letters go on either side

blocks.note: men are people
aid is help

explanation.surface: Bystanders gather round to assist a girl in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan shows the clue ends 'help a young girl'; the copy's 'a on girl' is an OCR slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is an old word for an unmarried girl or young woman.

clue.text: Old port for sailors

blocks.note: surface reading: a harbour town that has been in use for centuries
setter's reading: the left side of a ship, in the seaman's former word

explanation.walkthrough: Port here is the side of a ship, not a harbour; sailors once called that side by another name, dropped because it was too easily confused with starboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard was the traditional nautical term for the left-hand side of a vessel before port replaced it.

clue.text: The old man gets to notice morning

blocks.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
a.m. marks the morning

explanation.surface: Dad finally spots that it is morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old man' looks like father, but it is the 'old Adam', a phrase for the sinful nature of humanity, and Adam was the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam is the first and oldest man in the Bible, and the old Adam names inherited human nature.

clue.text: The coloured staff supplies an usher

blocks.note: black is a colour
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A painted stick provides someone to show guests to their seats.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Rod is the official of the House of Lords, properly the Gentleman Usher of the Black Rod, named after the ebony staff carried.
explanation.definitionFit: The parliamentary officer's full title makes this person literally an usher, carrying a dark staff of office.

clue.text: Tessa's useful qualities

blocks.note: the name and its possessive ending, letters only

explanation.surface: A woman named Tessa has some handy talents.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no anagram signal: the setter relies on the solver spotting the rearrangement unaided, which older puzzles sometimes allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are advantages or valuable attributes that a person can draw on.

clue.text: Barren recompense

blocks.note: first meaning: waterless and lifeless, as wasteland is
second meaning: what someone deserves

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently but spelt alike; the reward sense survives mainly in the phrase about just deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert as an adjective describes infertile empty land, and as a noun means a deserved reward or punishment.

clue.text: The worker is on edge in Ireland

definitions.note: A prepositional phrase stands for a place name here, fair because the answer is a county and the phrase points to somewhere situated in Ireland.

blocks.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A labourer is on the brink of something somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTRIM is a county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, so it is a location found within the island.

clue.text: Upsets a fool in the game

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside the other's letters

blocks.note: hares and hounds, a paper-chase game
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot playing in a match throws everyone off balance.
explanation.walkthrough: Hares and hounds is a cross-country chase game in which runners leave a paper trail.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass someone is to trouble and distress them persistently, which is what upsetting them repeatedly amounts to.

clue.text: As many fresh —— meet in one salt sea" (Henry V)

definitions.text: As many fresh —— meet in one salt sea" (Henry V)

blocks.clueFragment: As many fresh —— meet in one salt sea
blocks.note: surface reading: a line of Shakespeare with a word missing
setter's reading: the Archbishop of Canterbury's speech in act one, comparing many rivers flowing into the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: This is a quotation clue: supply the missing word from the play. Fresh waters flowing into a sea suggests running watercourses.
explanation.definitionFit: In the speech, many freshwater rivers and brooks are pictured joining a single ocean, the image filling the blank.

clue.text: You need a garment in the attempt to caricature

indicators.note: something in something else sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
taken as written
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: Advice that dressing up properly is required when trying to lampoon someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque or absurd imitation, which is what a caricature is.

clue.text: Goes on ice right after the fish

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: one who goes on ice

indicators.note: one piece coming after another means it is placed later in the answer

blocks.note: a skate is a flat ray fish
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A fish is put in the freezer straight after being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a verb but the answer is the person who does it, a loose fit common in older puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A skater is someone who glides across frozen surfaces on bladed boots.

clue.text: They renounce thraldom in song

blocks.note: surface reading: people who refuse to be enslaved
setter's reading: the patriotic anthem Rule, Britannia, whose refrain declares that a nation never shall be slaves

explanation.walkthrough: Rule, Britannia is an eighteenth-century British patriotic song whose chorus ends 'never, never, never shall be slaves'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's chorus names the inhabitants of Britain as those who will never submit to bondage.

clue.text: Find me round the current staff

indicators.note: going round something means wrapping around its letters

blocks.note: taken as written
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be located among the present employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a ceremonial staff of office carried before an official.

clue.text: Boredom can give place to sleep

indicators.note: can give suggests the word may be made to yield something else when its letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Being bored can send you off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom is the room in a house where people go to rest at night.

clue.text: Something to put forward for progress

definitions.text: Something to put forward for progress

blocks.note: surface reading: a proposal offered for consideration
setter's reading: the idiom about stepping out at one's most capable to advance

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'put your best foot forward' means to make the best possible effort; 'put forward' tempts toward a proposal or motion.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the limb one leads with when trying hardest, so it is literally put forward to get ahead.

clue.text: Transport borrowed for the fair

blocks.note: surface reading: a hired vehicle
setter's reading: the folk song Widecombe Fair, which opens with a request to lend an old horse for the journey

explanation.walkthrough: In the Devon folk song Widecombe Fair, Tom Pearce is asked to lend his horse so a crowd of friends can ride to the fair; it famously collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal borrowed from Tom Pearce in the song is a pale-coated female horse, the transport for the trip.

clue.text: Superficial appearances of teams when dismissed

indicators.note: when places the condition first in the reading, so the state described leads the answer

blocks.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
sides are teams

explanation.surface: Teams knocked out of a competition are judged on their looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Out is the cricket term for a batsman who has been dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Outsides are external surfaces, the way things look rather than what they are.

clue.text: Crustacea that keep to themselves

blocks.note: first meaning: hermit crabs, which live in borrowed shells
second meaning: recluses who live alone

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one description of shy shellfish, but the crabs and the recluses are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermit crabs are often called simply hermits, and the word's ordinary sense is solitary people living apart.

clue.text: Language found in an old city of the French

blocks.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
du is French for 'of the'

explanation.surface: A tongue unearthed in an ancient French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Toast for uncle

definitions.note: A phrase rather than a noun, fair because the security left with a pawnbroker is exactly the thing that is handed over for uncle.

blocks.note: first meaning: to drink someone's health
second meaning: an item left with a pawnbroker as security

explanation.walkthrough: Uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, so what is for him is the goods pawned.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge someone is to drink their health, and a pledge is also property deposited as security for a loan.

clue.text: The highest point of a river-horse

blocks.note: taken as written
the Po is Italy's longest river
gee or gee-gee is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: The peak of a hippopotamus, since hippopotamus means river-horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the furthest point of an orbit from Earth, hence any climax or summit.

clue.text: Provided the order is in — take a seat

indicators.note: one thing that is in another is placed inside its letters

blocks.note: to sit is to take a seat
Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: As long as your meal order has arrived, please sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the phrase SO BE IT, which in older English can mean 'on condition that'.
explanation.definitionFit: So be it once served as a conditional conjunction meaning on condition that, the sense of provided.

clue.text: A flying island

blocks.note: surface reading: something airborne
setter's reading: the floating island of scholars that Gulliver visits in Swift's satire

explanation.walkthrough: In Gulliver's Travels, Jonathan Swift describes an island that floats in the air by magnetism, inhabited by absent-minded theorists.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's fictional realm is a land mass that hovers above the ground, making it literally an airborne isle.

clue.text: Mark with a manuscript of contradictions

definitions.note: Opposites stand in for words of opposite meaning, fair because each pair of such words expresses a direct contrary of the other.

blocks.note: Mark Antony, the Roman general
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: Annotating a document full of inconsistencies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a verb for making a sign, but it is the first name of the Roman Mark Antony.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonyms are words opposite in sense, like hot and cold, each one contradicting its partner.

clue.text: Without the —— of some melodious tear" (Milton)

definitions.text: Without the —— of some melodious tear" (Milton)

blocks.clueFragment: Without the —— of some melodious tear
blocks.note: surface reading: a line of verse with a word missing
setter's reading: the line from Lycidas, the elegy for a drowned friend, about tribute owed to the dead

explanation.walkthrough: This is a quotation clue from Milton's elegy Lycidas: 'He must not float upon his watery bier unwept, and welter to the parching wind, without the ... of some melodious tear.'
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is an archaic term for a deserved reward or tribute, here the poem of mourning due to the dead.

clue.text: Zealous performer like Dorcas

blocks.note: surface reading: an enthusiastic actor or entertainer
setter's reading: the charitable woman in Acts, full of good works, so one who performs kind deeds

explanation.walkthrough: Dorcas (Tabitha) in the Acts of the Apostles is praised for her good works and almsgiving; 'performer' means one who performs deeds, not a stage artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer describes an earnest, sometimes over-eager philanthropist who busies themselves with charitable acts.

clue.text: Put back the chap in colour

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

blocks.note: red is a colour
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Restore the fellow to his painted state.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that remands a prisoner sends them back into custody until a later hearing.

clue.text: Smooth flow at close of day

blocks.note: even means smooth and level
a tide is a flow of the sea

explanation.surface: Calm currents running as the sun goes down.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the final part of the day.

clue.text: City for a female in the Women's Service

indicators.note: something in another thing sits within it, so these letters are placed inside

blocks.note: the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British army's women's branch in the Second World War
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A posting to some town for a woman serving in the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the women's branch of the British Army from 1938 to 1949.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital of Greece, a major European metropolis.
